purpose: The ways a running dart program can HOLD layer-1 content. Not layer 1 (the data is fixed), not layer 3 (no operations beyond load-and-read-back), not the type system.
reference: language knowledge, checked against ../type_vocabulary/raw/dart.types.json as a candidate checklist only (superseded node; not a decision instrument).

nothing.note: the single absence value, held in an untyped variable.
the type whose only value is null, named explicitly rather than inferred.
a normally-typed variable widened with ? to accept null alongside its usual values.

truth.note: two values, no numeric side in dart.

whole.note: on the native VM a signed 64-bit word that wraps past i64 edges; compiled to javascript the same code spells int as a double and erodes past 2^53 instead (dart-web finding, log_020) — this probe targets the native VM.
arbitrary-precision whole number holder, built from a decimal string rather than an integer literal.
IEEE double pressed into holding a whole number; exact only up to 2^53, so it erodes at the p53_plus1 and u64max edges even though it accepts the literal.

fractional.note: IEEE double, the default fractional holder.
the common super-type of int and double; a fractional literal picks the double branch at run time.

text.note: a run of utf-16 code units presented as unicode text; the default text holder.
utf-16 code units, not codepoints; a codepoint outside the basic plane is split into a surrogate pair.
unicode codepoints, not code units; recovers the clef as a single element instead of a surrogate pair.
a mutable text builder; holds the same content as String but changeable in place.

sequence.note: growable ordered run, one declared element kind.
length fixed at construction; growth operations refuse at run time even though element mutation still works.

probes.mixed: List<Object?> v = List<Object?>.from([1, "two", 3.0, true, null], growable: false);

sequence.note: unordered, no duplicates; kept in the table because that loss is the finding.
a read-only view; write operations refuse at run time, not at compile time.
fixed length, and each position may carry a different declared kind; the one dart sequence holder that takes the mixed row without widening to Object?.

keyed.note: name to element; dart's map literal is a LinkedHashMap by default, so insertion order is kept.
the same insertion-order holder spelled explicitly rather than via the map literal default.

probes.emptykey: LinkedHashMap<String, String> v = LinkedHashMap<String, String>.from({"": "empty-string key"});

keyed.note: the same grouping held in sorted key order rather than insertion order.

probes.emptykey: SplayTreeMap<String, String> v = SplayTreeMap<String, String>.from({"": "empty-string key"});

keyed.spelling: class R3 { final int a, b, c; R3(this.a, this.b, this.c); } R3(1, 2, 3)
keyed.note: names fixed when the shape is written, not when the data arrives; the odd keys (a digit, an empty string) are not spellable as dart field identifiers, so RI and RE are written honestly and left to refuse at compile time.

nesting.note: nesting by repeating the same holder; every level carries the same declared element kind unless widened.
values typed dynamic so each level may switch form freely.
every element widened to Object?; the dart holder that takes any layer-1 form in one position, which mixed nesting needs.

identity.note: dart lists hold references, so two positions can name one object.
built by copying rather than referencing; the contrast cell against the reference holders above.

identity.spelling: class Box { List<int> items; Box(this.items); } b = Box([1,2,3]); v = [b, b]
identity.pre:
class Box { List<int> items; Box(this.items); }
class Node { String name; Node? self; Node(this.name); }
identity.note: an ordinary mutable object reference; the class instance itself, not a field, is what two positions can share.
